title: Laurens van Hoepen moves to MP Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
MP Motorsport have confirmed the signing of Laurens van Hoepen for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

The 21-year-old is currently in the midst of his rookie campaign in F2 and has so far achieved a pole position as well as five podiums and is currently 10th in the Standings with two rounds to go.

Prior to this year, Van Hoepen spent two seasons in Formula 3 and scored five podiums during that time.

The Dutch driver will now join forces with Dutch outfit in 2027, and at the announcement, he revealed his delight at getting the chance to race for his home team.

“It’s good to finally join forces with a team that has been on my doorstep since my karting days,” said Van Hoepen. “I have witnessed their incredible success first-hand, especially in my last five seasons in FRECA and FIA F3, and with the experience of a season of Formula 2 under my belt, I’m confident that I can add more prizes to their impressive trophy cabinet.

“MP is a team of many nationalities now, but it still feels like a natural move to join the home team and race in the orange home colours.”

MP Motorsport Team Principal Sander Dorsman also added: “I’m incredibly pleased that Laurens has become a member of our MP family. A Dutch driver with a Dutch team is always going to be special, and with Laurens’ obvious talent and the debut season that he’s had, it was a matter of time before we put two and two together. With Laurens on board as the first of our F2 drivers, we are aiming to continue our frontrunning F2 form in 2027.”

title: Points in Baku debut weekend ‘more than we expected’ says Yamakoshi
excerpt:
Hiyu Yamakoshi made his FIA Formula 2 debut in Baku last time out, and afterwards he reflected on his weekend with Van Amersfoort Racing.

The Japanese driver qualified 18th and after taking the chequered flag in P17 in the Sprint returned on Friday afternoon to score his first point in P9 in Feature Race 1.

Yamakoshi then finished 14th in Feature Race 2, and speaking at the end of it all, he was fairly happy with how things went in Azerbaijan.

“In the end, I just got in the points, which was more than what we expected overall,” said Yamakoshi. “After a difficult qualifying, it was more difficult than I expected but it was my second ever time driving in F2.

“But I’m happy with the weekend. I learned so many things, I made progress on many things, especially for Feature Race 1 with the Supersoft. My best lap was only half a second from down, and actually pretty much same as Martinius, which is like around top five pace.

Yamakoshi reflected on his first weekend in Formula 2 in Baku

“I impressed myself. Today we were struggling a bit with the balance of the car, but still, I think my pace was around top ten. Before the pit stop, I overtook Bilinski as well, so for me overall the weekend was really positive and nice progress overall.”

On a weekend where the drivers had three races, Yamakoshi picked a few things he learned while racing wheel-to-wheel, and he also explained how racing Formula 3 helped him to prepare for the challenge of Baku.

Brando Badoer steps up with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

Noah Stromsted completes Invicta Racing lineup for 2027 season

“I mean, of course, the rest of the drivers have more experience in Formula 2, so I have a bit of a disadvantage,” he said. “But I think F3 has more fights, with the race starts and the slipstream, the tow effect is big.

“So, I learned a lot this year, especially from Monza, and I just used that experience in Baku as well.”

The Japanese driver talked about what he learned in Baku

Yamakoshi continued to pick out a few things he experienced for the first time, such as pistops and strategies.

“The pitstops were the difficult part,” said Yamakoshi. “I still have to learn how to drive on the limit right way, especially with the colder tyre on the out lap, because I lost around 1.5 or two seconds in the out lap, so I have to improve.

“Of course, it's my first time proper pushing on an out lap, so if I have another chance, I can be better. Also, this is a city track, a street track, and the wall is just next to me, if I go over the limit then I’m in the wall which is not the best.

“So, I took a little bit of margin, I didn't take risks, but if I have another chance at a track like Yas Marina or Qatar, I think I can take a bit more risk, so it should be a little bit better.”

title: Brando Badoer steps up with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport have confirmed the signing of Brando Badoer for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Badoer steps up to F2 after a strong 2026 campaign with Rodin in Formula 3, finishing eighth in the Drivers’ Standings. The Italian achieved four podiums this season, including a Feature Race victory in Monte Carlo.

Prior to that, Badoer finished sixth in the 2023 Formula 4 UAE, Italian F4 and Euro 4 Championships.

In 2024, the 20-year-old also finished fifth in the Formula Regional European Championship and fourth in the 2025 Formula Regional Middle East Championship.

Badoer now continues his rise up the single seater ladder with Rodin, and at the announcement, he expressed how excited he was to continue with the team in Formula 2.

“I’m really happy to be announced as a Formula 2 driver for Rodin Motorsport," said Badoer. "I’m grateful to the team for the opportunity and the trust they’ve put in me, and after such a great season together, I’m excited to continue this journey.

"I really feel like Rodin is a family, so I’m looking forward to working with the F2 team, building on what we’ve achieved and creating more great moments together.”

Rodin Motorsport Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “I’m delighted to continue our relationship with Brando as he takes the next step into FIA Formula 2 next season. He’s shown great progress throughout his first season with the team, securing a race win at Monaco and multiple podiums along the way, while playing a key role in leading our F3 campaign. His performances have shown what he’s capable of and we’re looking forward to seeing him build on that experience as he continues his career in Formula 2.”

title: Noah Stromsted completes Invicta Racing lineup for 2027 season
excerpt:
Invicta Racing has confirmed that Noah Stromsted will join the team in 2027.

The British outfit is the first team to finalise its plans for next season, with the Dane joining 2026 FIA Formula 3 teammate Freddie Slater at Invicta.

Stromsted makes the step up to F2 after finishing 10th in the FIA F3 Standings this season, earning a victory at the Red Bull Ring.

On his joining Invicta in F2 next year, Stromsted said he was looking forward to working with such a successful team and was eager to get going with preparations for the 2027 campaign.

“I’m really excited to be stepping up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year. I’ve learned a great deal competing in FIA Formula 3 since 2024 and I feel ready to take on the next challenge in my career. Over the past few seasons, Invicta Racing has established itself as the performance benchmark on the F2 grid and I’m looking forward to getting to know everyone in the team. I can’t wait to start preparing for 2027 and I’m excited to see what we can achieve together.”

James Robinson, CEO & Team Principal of Invicta Racing added: “We’re delighted to welcome Noah to Invicta Racing for the 2027 season. FIA Formula 3 is one of the most competitive categories in junior single-seater motorsport and, after following his progress closely, we believe that Noah has all the qualities to be a future champion, so we’re very much looking forward to helping him make the step up to Formula 2. With Noah and Freddie [Slater] working alongside each other, I’m very excited to see what we can achieve.”

title: FIA Formula 2 Championship announce 2027 season calendar
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 2 Championship has announced today its 2027 calendar, featuring 14 rounds across Asia, Oceania, Europe and the American continent, with two new venues joining the schedule and the return of Montreal, after its successful addition to the 2026 season.

The 2027 season will welcome Istanbul and Mexico City to the F2 calendar, with both events taking place in October. Their addition creates a more balanced championship schedule, reducing the previously extended gap ahead of the final two rounds in Lusail and Yas Island.

The 2027 campaign will get underway in Sakhir, Bahrain, in March, alongside Formula 1, before the field heads directly to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, one week later. From there, the Championship will travel to Melbourne, Australia, before going to Montreal, Canada.

The European leg to the season will begin in June at Monaco, home to one of the most prestigious rounds of the year, as well as one of the most challenging circuits on the calendar. The action will then continue in July at Silverstone, Great Britain, and Spielberg, Austria, back-toback before the summer break.

September will provide a thrilling three-round stretch, beginning at Monza, Italy, followed by Madrid, Spain, and concluding at the Baku City Circuit in Azerbaijan.

In October, Formula 2 will visit Istanbul, Türkiye, for its first race weekend at the demanding circuit, which is making its return to the Formula 1 calendar. The Championship will then head to Mexico City, Mexico, for another highly anticipated new addition to the calendar.

The addition of Mexico City to the F2 calendar was confirmed today during a press conference attended by FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel, Alejandra Frausto, Ministry of Tourism of Mexico City, Formula 1 Gran Premio de la ciudad de Mexico Managing Director Federico Gonzalez Compean and FIA Formula 2 drivers Rafael Villagomez and Noel Leon.

The 2027 season will conclude in December with two consecutive race weekends, first at Lusail, Qatar, before the Championship travels to Yas Island, UAE, for the season finale.

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA President said: ““The 2027 FIA Formula 2 Championship calendar reflects the continued strength and global growth of an important championship at the heart of our driver development pathway. The addition of Istanbul and Mexico City will bring Formula 2 to new audiences and give the next generation of talent the opportunity to compete on an even greater variety of circuits around the world. Alongside the return to Montreal, these additions further strengthen a truly international calendar across four continents. “I look forward to another exciting season and to seeing the stars of the future continue their journey towards the highest levels of our sport.”

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1 said: “The 2027 FIA Formula 2 calendar will deliver another exciting season of racing across 14 rounds at some of the most iconic and challenging venues in world motorsport, including the addition of Istanbul and Mexico City. Formula 2 continues to play a vital role as the ultimate pathway to Formula 1, giving the most promising young drivers the opportunity to compete on the same stage as the pinnacle of our sport and showcase their talent to fans, teams and partners around the world. Year after year, the Championship delivers outstanding racing and helps develop the next generation of Formula 1 stars. I would like to thank the FIA President and their entire team, Bruno Michel and his team, as well as all our promoters, partners, officials, marshals and volunteers whose dedication and commitment make this Championship possible. I look forward to following another highly competitive season in 2027."

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 2 CEO said: “I’m very excited to add three new venues in a financially sustainable way, with the return of Montreal following its surprise addition in 2026 and the first appearance of Istanbul and Mexico City. We will be covering freight costs so that the territorial expansion of the calendar does not financially impact our teams. With a calendar spanning four continents and a carefully distributed sequence of Rounds, the 2027 FIA formula 2 Championship will offer teams and drivers a demanding and diverse season, while bringing the category to new audiences and strengthening its position as a global platform for the next generation of Formula 1 talent.”

title: Joshua Duerksen joins Hitech for 2027 F2 season
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Joshua Duerksen will join the team for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

The Paraguayan is the first driver to be confirmed as part of the British team's line-up for next year, joining after three years of experience in the F2 Championship.

He debuted in F2 back in 2024, and since then has secured eight victories in the Championship along with 16 podiums in total.

Ahead of the move to Hitech, the Mercedes Development Driver said that he was very excited to be moving to the team for next season.

“I’m incredibly excited to be joining Hitech for the 2027 Formula 2 season.

“Hitech has shown for many years that it is one of the strongest teams in Formula 2 and I’m very proud to have the opportunity to race with them. I’m looking forward to getting to know everyone, starting the work together and seeing what we can achieve.

“The new car for 2027 gives us another exciting challenge and I’m really motivated to get started. I want to keep developing, keep fighting for wins and the best results possible on all tracks. I’m confident that together we can achieve some great things next season.”

Jan Sumann, Hitech’s F2 Head of Race Engineering added: “We’re very pleased to welcome Joshua to Hitech for 2027. He’s a proven Formula 2 race winner and we’ve seen first-hand from the pit wall the speed and race craft he brings.

“He has continued to develop throughout his time in the championship and has shown that he can deliver results and perform under pressure. He brings valuable experience with him, particularly as we head into 2027 and the challenge of understanding the evolution of the F2 car.

“Joshua is ambitious, motivated and has already achieved a great deal in Formula 2, but it’s clear that he is hungry for more. We’re looking forward to working with him and seeing what we can achieve together next season.”

title: Bruno Michel's Baku Debrief
excerpt:
It was an important weekend in the fight for the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Championship as we had a bumper weekend in Baku with two Qualifying sessions and Feature Races.

FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel talks about how the organisation of the round came together and gave his thoughts on the action that unfolded on three consequential days in the 2026 title race.

DOUBLING UP IN BAKU

"We wanted to do that because there was only Formula 2 as a support race here, and for the fans and for the promoter, it was good to be able to increase the number of races that we were having. It was easy to organize, too.

"This is a great track that the drivers really love. It's very demanding and it's very spectacular as well, and having three races here was good.

"I think we've shown that this format is working very well when there is enough track time to be able to do that. So, we'll keep it in mind for the future."

THE TITLE BATTLE KEEPS EVERYONE GUESSING

"The whole weekend was very dramatic. Rodin was flying here in terms of performance. It was quite impressive what they did in Qualifying between Dunne and Stenshorne - 1-2, 2-1 - and they've done an absolutely fantastic job.

"Alex was just untouchable in the first Feature Race, and in the Sprint Race, he was very impressive, too. On the other hand, Nikola Tsolov, who arrived in Baku as a leader, had a very difficult day. And he had an even more complicated time after he picked up a grid penalty for the second Feature Race, having then to start from P11.

"Rafael Câmara did better than Tsolov. He scored strong points in the first Feature Race, but he was in an even better form in Feature Race 2.

What we learned in Baku: The title fight hots up but who has the momentum?

TITLE FIGHT ANALYSIS: How Baku showed that the championship fight is far from over

"That third race was everything you want to see in terms of motor racing. When you have three drivers fighting for the championship, fighting on track for the first three places and all of them on the podium… It was fantastic to watch!

"It's a bit too bad for Alex, because a couple of mistakes cost him dearly. But he was there and he was extremely fast. He cut the line first and classified third. His great weekend in Baku means that he’s moved up to third and he’s closed in on the top 2 in the Standings, with two rounds to go.

"Rafael had a very strong race on Saturday, he did what he had to do, and he was handed the win, which takes him to the top of the Championship. In the meantime, Nikola did not give up. Starting from P11, he put his head down. Ultimately, together with his team, they had a good strategy and the VSC and Safety Car timing worked in their favor. In the end, he did a fantastic race to take P2.

“Seeing the three of them finishing within three seconds and seeing the top three of them on the podium is very, very, very exciting. It's a great way to continue this season ahead of the next two events."

THE TEAMS' STANDINGS CLOSES UP

"Campos Racing has been showing what they can do in Formula 3 and now they're up there in Formula 2 and they're leading the Championship with two strong drivers.

"Invicta Racing has been winning in F2 the last two championships so it's no surprise they're up there as well. We know they're good, and we know they're a very solid team.

"As for Rodin Motorsport, what they have achieved this week in Baky is really impressive, with both of their drivers. They’ve had the pace in Qualifying all season long. Now they found the pace during the races, too.

"It's all done in a very competitive but very good spirit as well, which is the way F2 is. The teams are all fighting extremely competitively on the track. But everybody is respectful of the others and same thing for the drivers.

"There's drama on the track but never outside the track and I think that's really what we want to see in this Championship. We're looking forward to being in Qatar and to be in Abu Dhabi for the end of this thriller."

title: What we learned in Baku: The title fight hots up but who has the momentum?
excerpt:
Round 12 has come and gone and we have a new Championship leader, but while Rafael Câmara is the driver everyone is now aiming for, is he the man in form?

That and more in what we learned across the Baku weekend…

THE TITLE FIGHT MOMENTUM ISN’T WITH THE LEADER

If you thought this was a title fight between just two drivers, you’ll want to reconsider. Alexaner Dunne put together arguably his finest round in FIA Formula 2 so far to well and truly stake his claim over the 2026 Drivers’ title.

The Rodin Motorsport driver entered the weekend 38 points adrift of then-points leader, Nikola Tsolov. He leaves Baku 18 back from Rafael Câmara after the Brazilian took over at the top of the leaderboard.

And even after taking 20 points out of the deficit, the Irishman left Baku dejected after feeling he should have been even closer, but for a misjudgment entering the pit lane in Feature Race 2 that netted him a five-second time penalty, demoting him from the top step to third.

Four consecutive podium finishes and a scoring streak going back a further three races proves that he is hitting form at the perfect moment.

The Alpine Academy driver also earned his first pole of the season having been a near constant presence in the top three on a Friday so far this season.

Though Câmara will have left Baku the happiest of the three contenders, it’s no longer just Tsolov who is the major threat to him in the title fight. Dunne means business and if he keeps his Baku form going into Lusail, he’s the driver to keep an eye on.

Dunne and Camara were Feature Race winners in Baku and both look set to fight to the wire for the 2026 crown

CÂMARA BRINGS THE CONSISTENCY

Câmara took the lead of the F2 Drivers’ Standings for the first time in 2026 with his Baku Feature Race 2 victory.

The Brazilian has a seven-point advantage over Tsolov leaving Azerbaijan, and now has three Feature wins this season, one shy of the Bulgarian’s tally so far in 2026.

The P15 result in the Sprint Race was the first non-score in a race the Ferrari Driver Academy talent has finished since all the way back at the start of July in the Silverstone Sprint.

His near constant presence in the scoring positions in the intervening races, minus one DNF in the Monza Sprint, has helped him fight back in the title race.

TITLE FIGHT ANALYSIS: How Baku showed that the championship fight is far from over

Stenshorne pleased with comeback performance in Baku after tough run of results

That consistency has finally rewarded him with the lead of the Championship heading into Round 13 in Lusail.

Tsolov, meanwhile, has comparatively been in a slump in form after his heights of back-to-back wins at Silverstone and a podium in Spa.

His Saturday fightback in the second Baku Feature Race limited what looked likely to be a major points swing, but he will need to start finding the same vein of form as earlier in the season to keep Câmara under pressure now he’s out in front.

RODIN AND DAMS ON THE RISE

Beganovic's Baku form was further demonstration that DAMS has taken a big step forward recently

In the past two rounds, four teams have taken victories: Hitech, Invicta Racing, Rodin Motorsport and DAMS Lucas Oil.

The latter two have improved their championship standing in the process. DAMS now resides fifth in the Teams’ Standings having overtaken ART Grand Prix, while Rodin sits third after climbing ahead of MP Motorsport and is just a single point behind Invicta Racing.

Dino Beganovic has enjoyed a climb up the Drivers’ Championship himself, now sitting in the top five having earned 58 points across the last two rounds.

The Swede’s teammate Roman Bilinski is also on a run of four-consecutive points finishes in his own right. Meanwhile, Rodin’s Martinius Stenshorne earned pole for Feature Race 2 in Baku, secured a podium in the first Feature of the weekend and is on a points run of his own stretching back five races.

Both teams are on the up at a crucial time in the season, and with two rounds to go, both look well-placed to add another victory to their 2026 tallies before the end.

title: Stenshorne pleased with comeback performance in Baku after tough run of results
excerpt:
Martinius Stenshorne was pleased with how his Baku weekend went overall, although he was slightly disappointed not to have converted pole position into a victory in Feature Race 2.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was in brilliant form throughout the three days in Azerbaijan, following up his P2 in Qualifying 1 with pole in Qualifying 2 by 0.445s.

Stenshorne then finished fourth in the Sprint Race, before taking second in Feature Race 1.

However, in the final race of the weekend, the Norwegian dropped to third behind teammate Alexander Dunne and Rafael Câmara during the pitstop phase, before being overtaken by Nikola Tsolov.

Stenshorne took the chequered flag in fourth, and speaking afterwards, he admitted that there were mixed feelings with his results.

“Overall it's been a positive weekend,” said Stenshorne. “I think we were quick in qualifying, quick in practice, and quick in the Sprint and Feature Race. But we missed a bit today, to be honest.

Stenshorne was very happy to be fighting at the front in Baku

“We made some changes that didn't fully work out. We were just lacking a little bit and then that was enough to take us off the podium. Anyway, I think we have to be happy with the weekend.

“A lot of points scored, moved up some positions as well in the championship, so we're pretty pleased.”

TITLE FIGHT ANALYSIS: How Baku showed that the championship fight is far from over

Chasing the Dream Season 8 Episode 13 – Out Today

When asked why he and Rodin chose to make some changes after a strong performance on Friday, Stenshorne explained that the nature of the track means that they are constantly having to adapt their car.

“The track is evolving all the time,” he explained.” Obviously, the street circuit is not being run at so much, so the track is constantly changing. I think we were really quick in the Sprint Race.

“We lacked maybe a little bit in the Feature Race 1 and then a bit more again now in the second Feature.

The Rodin Motorsport driver shared why he and the team chose to make changes to their car

“There are some things that we could have done better but overall I think we have to be really happy with our weekend. I think qualifying, especially Qualifying 2 was amazing, so really happy about that.”

The Norwegian has been a constant presence in the points in recent rounds – scoring points in six out of the last eight races.

‘We’re definitely in the fight’ says Dunne after race-winning Baku weekend

‘It was much more than a win’ says Tsolov after comeback to second in Baku Feature Race 2

But Stenshorne was delighted to be back fighting at the front of the field in Baku, with the results also helping him go from 11th to seventh in the Drivers’ Standings at the end of the weekend.

“Obviously it was good, it was a weekend where we had a lot of running as well,” he continued. “There was a lot of points that we could take and we took a lot, so that was quite positive for the championship side as well.

“But obviously we wanted more starting first today, but anyway it was a good comeback from some difficult rounds.”
